stem:
Bharat hangs a metal pot from a spring balance and reads the scale.

What does this reading measure?

options.text: The weight of the pot — the pull of the Earth on the pot — in newtons.
The mass of the pot in kilograms.
Stretching the spring further increases the Earth's pull on the same pot.
The downward push of Bharat's hand on the pot is the pot's weight.

teacher.key_rationale: Weight is the gravitational pull of Earth on the pot and is measured in newtons. Kilograms name mass instead of weight. Claiming a longer stretch increases Earth's pull on the same pot reverses the force-stretch reading. Calling Bharat's hand push the pot's weight mis-scopes weight.
